text: 🇲🇽🎨 "Public education is the same for the landowner as for the field hand." "Our obligation is for the public school to be the best — and it already is, even better than private. Adjusting for socioeconomic level, public schools scored better than private ones." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on education On the PISA results: she credits the teaching corps vilified during the neoliberal education reform, and notes the test recognizes Mexico's reduced educational inequality.

🇲🇽✊ "GDP grew 1% under López Obrador — and 13.5 million families rose out of poverty." "The problem isn't only growth, but the distribution of wealth: wages, well-being programs and public works distribute it. That's why we must speak of development, not just growth." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on development vs growth Rebutting analysts fixated on GDP figures; she frames wages, well-being programs and public investment as the mechanism that distributes the gains.

🏠🇲🇽 "Gentrification is displacing those who originally lived in a place." "...so people of another economic level move in, with housing priced so only a small percentage can afford it. Some governments drive it with corruption, like the Benito Juárez real-estate cartel that violated land-use rules through officials' bribes." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on gentrification On foreigners earning in dollars and spending in pesos displacing residents in Mexico City, Guadalajara, Tijuana and the Riviera Maya. Her answer: the state builds social housing to pull private prices down.

🔥🇲🇽 "They are not information media, they are propaganda media." "Many outlets in Mexico have one objective: to be propaganda for the right. They have a group chat where they agree on what they'll all say that week. Their objective is to return to the past of corruption and privilege." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the press Responding to columnists dismissing Mexico's internal-market-driven growth and to the week's coordinated attack lines.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>A Record July: 4.41 Million Tourists Chose Mexico</u>

Mexico drew 4.41 million international tourists in July, up 3.8% year-on-year and a record for the month, per INEGI's traveler survey — total international visitors reached 8.65 million (+2.9%), with border tourism surging 13.2%. The country the US State Department keeps slapping with travel warnings just posted its busiest July on record.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>The Country That Believes in Trains Again</u>

Mexico will open the AIFA–Pachuca passenger train in 2027, a 58-km line built to move over 100,000 riders a day at 120 km/h, President Sheinbaum confirmed — part of a public rail revival that also includes the México–Querétaro and Saltillo–Nuevo Laredo routes. Forty years after the neoliberals scrapped passenger rail and sold off the tracks, the state is laying them back down.

🇲🇽📉 <u>13.4 Million Lifted Out of Poverty — Facts, Not Charity</u>

Between 2018 and 2024, 13.4 million Mexicans exited poverty and the rate fell from 41.9% to 29.6%, per INEGI — the result of a minimum wage up 154% in real terms and roughly 1 trillion pesos a year in welfare reaching 42.8 million people. The neoliberals called redistribution "populism." Mexico calls it the largest poverty drop in its modern history.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>The Admirals Ran the Fuel Racket — Now the State Is Prosecuting It</u>

Mexico's FGR confirmed that ex-admirals Roberto and Fernando Farías Laguna — "Los Primos" — headed one of the country's biggest "huachicol fiscal" networks, moving fuel shipped from Texas and mislabeled as additives to dodge taxes, with 10 million liters of diesel seized on a single ship at Altamira. They rigged promotions inside the Navy and customs across five states to keep it running. The rot reached the top brass, and this is the government dragging it into court.

🇲🇽🏠 <u>Housing as a Right, Not a Mortgage Trap</u>

Sheinbaum's Vivienda para el Bienestar aims to reach 12 million families this term: 1.8 million new homes built directly by the state, 5.2 million unpayable credits inherited from the neoliberal era restructured, and a million property titles handed to families who never had papers. Already 667,000 homes are contracted — 37% of the goal — and the program alone adds about 1.2% to annual GDP. Housing built for people to live in, not for banks to foreclose on.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>State-Owned, Not Sold Off: Mexico Bankrolls Its Own Trains</u>

While neoliberals spent 30 years privatizing everything that moved, Mexico's 2027 budget puts 44 billion pesos into four state companies it refuses to sell — 25 billion for the Interoceanic Train, 18.1 billion for the Tren Maya, nearly 900 million for the revived Mexicana de Aviación (a 700% jump), plus funds to keep LitioMx and its nationalized lithium in public hands. The infrastructure belongs to the nation, and the nation is paying to keep it that way.
